newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rebel on secret visit from France - paper.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rebel on secret visit from France - paper.

text.p: A Tamil Tiger rebel leader has secretly arrived in northern Sri Lanka from France to try to broker a deal to end the Indian Ocean island's ethnic war, two newspapers said on Sunday.

Lawrence Thilakar, the Paris-based international spokesman for the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE), had come to brief LTTE chief Velupillai Prabhakaran on possible moves to resume peace talks, the independent Sunday Times said.
"...Thilakar has secretly come to Sri Lanka in what is seen as a move to broker a peace deal with international support," the newspaper said in its lead story, quoting political sources.
Sri Lankan government officials were not available to comment.

Diplomats said it was unlikely Sri Lanka would accept third party mediation to help end the rebels' war for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the north and east as the government had rejected previous such offers.
LTTE officials in London said Anton Rajah, another rebel spokesman, was not immediately available for comment.
The Sunday Times said Thilakar had come via Nepal and across India under a false name.
The independent Sunday Leader newspaper said Thilakar had arrived on a rebel- owned cargo ship and been picked up by rebel boats off the northwestern Mannar area.
The newspaper said Thilakar had held talks with Western political leaders who had pledged their support for fresh peace talks. It did not say who the leaders were.
Sri Lankan President Chandrika Kumaratunga recently said she was confident of finishing the war by the year's end because of a series of successful military campaigns against the rebels.
The rebels have been confined to jungle bases since government forces ousted them from their northern Jaffna peninsula stronghold early last year.
The Defence Ministry said last week that 200 rebels and 65 soldiers were killed during an attack on Thursday on the Vaunathivu army camp in Batticaloa, about 200 km (125 miles) from Colombo.
The Tigers said only 84 rebel fighters were killed.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died since the civil war began in 1983.
